title: ASM-inspection convention + asm-artefact-present gate
description:
Establish the per-kernel `*.asm.txt` artefact convention and register the `asm-artefact-present` JIT gate. Reviewers use these artefacts to confirm SIMD/ILP transforms actually emitted the expected mnemonics.

## Background

The PPC spiral makes specific claims at each step (e.g., "V3 SIMD via VPCLMULQDQ", "V2 ILP with 8 independent accumulators"). Without a committed asm artefact, reviewers have to regenerate disassembly themselves to verify each claim. This task:

1. Adds `dev/scripts/regen-asm.sh <crate> <symbol> <output-path> [extra-symbol …]` wrapping `cargo show-asm -p <crate> --simplify <symbol>` with a metadata header recording **crate, primary symbol, extra symbols, output path, rustc version, host triple, target-cpu, RUSTFLAGS, git commit SHA, regeneration timestamp (UTC), and tool used (cargo-show-asm vs. fallback)**. The git commit SHA is the canonical "is this artefact still current?" indicator; the timestamp is informational.
2. Establishes the convention that each new SIMD kernel has a sibling `<kernel-name>.asm.txt` artefact in `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/x86/asm/`. Per-fn artefacts (`<module>_<fn>.asm.txt`) are also accepted by the gate.
3. Registers the `asm-artefact-present` gate (auto, postcheck, runs `./scripts/asm-artefact-present.sh`) which fails if any `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/x86/*.rs` file (excluding `mod.rs`) modified at HEAD lacks a corresponding sibling `*.asm.txt` modification *in the same commit*. The "co-modified" semantics enforce that every spiral-step regenerates the artefact rather than leaving a stale one in place.
4. Documents the convention in `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/README.md`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] `dev/scripts/regen-asm.sh` runs `cargo show-asm` successfully on at least one existing SIMD symbol; metadata header includes git commit SHA, rustc version, and host triple (date alone is insufficient — the commit SHA is the reproducibility anchor).
- [hard] JIT gate `asm-artefact-present` registered with `auto: true, stage: postcheck`.
- [hard] Sample artefact `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/x86/asm/avx2_xor.asm.txt` committed alongside this task to demonstrate the convention.
- [hard] README documents the regeneration procedure and what the gate enforces.

## Verification (post-merge)

The gate runner was exercised in a temp test repo against 8 scenarios — all pass:

| # | Scenario | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A | No SIMD changes | vacuous pass |
| B | `.rs` added without `.asm.txt` | FAIL with clear error |
| C | Exact `<module>.asm.txt` match | PASS |
| D | Per-fn `<module>_<fn>.asm.txt` match | PASS |
| E | Only `mod.rs` modified | vacuous pass (mod.rs excluded) |
| F | Multi-file partial coverage | FAIL, names the uncovered file |
| G | `.rs` modified, `.asm.txt` NOT co-modified in same commit | FAIL (co-modification enforced) |
| H | Fresh repo (no HEAD~1) | defensive vacuous pass |

## Notes

Spec doc: attached as `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`. Out-of-scope follow-up: bug `1d230525` tracks a duplicate `--out-dir` flag in the `REGEN_ASM_FALLBACK=1` path (primary cargo-show-asm path is unaffected).
